what_it_does: Federated learning is a way to train an AI model across many devices — like phones or sensors — without sending anyone's raw data to a central server; instead, each device trains a local copy and sends back only the adjustments (gradients) it learned. The problem is that those adjustment packages are large, and devices with slow or metered network connections cannot keep up. This paper proposes a framework where each device watches how similar its local updates are to the global model's direction, and only transmits compressed updates when that similarity drops below a threshold — in other words, when it actually has something meaningfully new to say. This adaptive gating is claimed to cut communication load significantly on constrained embedded devices. The approach is described at the abstract level and the exact compression scheme and full empirical results require the full paper to evaluate.
